hints: Focus on what controls gas density when temperature and pressure are the same, think about mass per mole of mixture.
Notice the molar masses are very different, with $\text{CH}_4$ at 16 much heavier than $\text{H}_2$ at 2 and $\text{He}$ at 4, so even a small % of methane matters a lot.
Calculate the weighted average molar mass for each planet using % by molecules as mole fraction, and pick the largest average mass.
walkthrough:
**Link density to average molar mass**

For gases compared under the same conditions, density is proportional to mass per mole. A heavier average mole means a denser gas.

$$\text{density} \propto \text{average } M_r$$

**Write the weighted average expression**

Because % is by number of molecules, it is the same as % by moles. So multiply each % by its molar mass.

$$\text{average } M_r = \frac{(\% \text{H}_2 \times 2) + (\% \text{He} \times 4) + (\% \text{CH}_4 \times 16)}{100}$$

**Compare the mixtures**

$\text{CH}_4$ ($M_r = 16$) is much heavier than $\text{H}_2$ ($M_r = 2$) and $\text{He}$ ($M_r = 4$). Uranus has the most $\text{CH}_4$ at 2.3% while still keeping a high % of $\text{He}$.

$$\text{Uranus: } (82.5 \times 2) + (15.2 \times 4) + (2.3 \times 16) = 262.6$$
This gives average $M_r = 2.626$, higher than Jupiter (2.20), Saturn (2.12) and Neptune (2.52). So Uranus has the greatest density.

options.A: Jupiter is mostly light $\text{H}_2$ (89.8%) with some $\text{He}$ and no $\text{CH}_4$. Its average $M_r$ is about 2.20, which is lighter than the mixtures containing heavy methane.
options.B: Neptune has more $\text{He}$ and 1.0% $\text{CH}_4$, giving an average $M_r$ of about 2.52. This is dense, but its methane content is less than half that of Uranus, so it is not the densest.
options.C: Saturn has the most $\text{H}_2$ (96.3%), the lightest gas. Its average $M_r$ is only about 2.12, the lowest of the four, so it gives the lowest density.
options.D: Uranus has 82.5% $\text{H}_2$, 15.2% $\text{He}$ and the highest % of heavy $\text{CH}_4$ at 2.3%. Its weighted average $M_r$ is about 2.63, the largest value, so at the same conditions it has the greatest density.
